terms.comment: With a hook, uncō affīgere: uncō is the ablative, “with a hook”, or the dative, “to a hook”, as the context decides. Affīgere is to fasten or attach, not every sense of English “hook”: choose the verb by the action and its result.

evidence: Verg. G. 2.389: oscilla ex altā suspendunt mollia pīnū
terms.comment: For hooking something over a bar and leaving it hanging, as in the composed example of the stick on the scaffolding; compare Vergil for suspendere ex + ablative. trānsversārium is Vitruvius’s crosspiece; a scaffold tube is not a vectis (lever, crowbar).

phrases.english: Hook this onto this hook / attach this to this hook.

phrases.latin: Theodōrus bacillum aduncum ex trānsversāriō māchinae suspendit.
phrases.english: Theo hung the hooked stick from the scaffold’s crossbar.

sources: Lewis & Short: affigo · Lewis & Short: suspendo · Lewis & Short: transversarius
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
